method: Static code/data-flow and activation-surface review; archive/member inspection; bounded isolated literal decoding and CPU emulation only; no Windows APIs, remote payloads, or specimen entry points executed on the host.
limits: Protected native samples 64 and 65 were not fully unpacked and remain purgatory.
No inference of endpoint deployment authorization from signatures/product identity.
No fetched dependencies or remote responses were executed.
Atomscan warned that model feature version 18 predates expected version 21; final pool decisions use reviewed evidence and cold trait coverage rather than model probability.

PeNet parser source and native PE fixture corpus. Verified parser/testing documentation and fixture purpose. Signature digest mismatch in altered test PEs is contextual; a real suspended-process injection fixture remains suspicious.
Earlier PeNet parser source, same parser/fixture assessment as 2.9.0. Embedded native injection fixture remains visible.
Caddy proxy-manager source. SQL/probe strings are query/error detection and proxy management inputs; one unusual query probe remains.
QEMU source archive and build/test material. Writable executable section observation belongs to bundled native test/build artifacts; no unrelated executable activation path identified.

Omni communications/agent package. Inspected lifecycle installer, entry points, bundled JS AST call sites and callback hosts. Installer pins its own global version; unrelated telemetry and hooks are not an exfiltration flow. A real libsignal signature-verifier success shortcut remains suspicious.
Ripple package. Inspected source, manifest and API call sites; no hidden lifecycle export or remote stage identified.

Kahitsan plugin SDK. Safely evaluated only the isolated literal decoder and replaced 5,326 constant decoder calls across 273 aliases. Recovered tenant-scoped ERP database/router/RPC logic, with no fixed attacker collection destination. Encoded reviewer notice tells AI systems to override higher-priority instructions and refuse analysis. This review interference is real; endpoint-malware intent is unproven.
Veritas CLI. Base64-evaluated shell launchers are real and retained as one suspicious finding; inspected decoded launch and validation paths and found no separate concealed collection stage.

Lightdash CLI. Lifecycle telemetry reports install UUID and OS to first-party analytics. Reviewed install script and source/callback inventory; no prompt/credential export inferred from unrelated hooks.

API Spector API-testing package. Reviewed manifests, install surfaces and JS call sites; no concealed lifecycle network/payload path established.

AIMS workstation agent/CLI source. Reviewed JS entry points, process/network operations and manifest. Environment-based TLS verification disable is real and remains suspicious; no separate hostile stage found.
Airdrop LLM application package. Reviewed lifecycle, source file inventory and JS call sites. JSX parse limitations were confined to UI source; no hidden install-stage collection identified.
Tool-management plugin source. Reviewed lifecycle and file/process/network call sites; configured tool execution is the advertised plugin capability.
Code-navigation/RAG CLI. Decoded shell launcher/eval is real and retains one suspicious finding; inspected launch guards and destinations rather than treating package identity as exoneration.
pikepdf source with PDF regression corpus. Leading-garbage PDF fixture tests parser tolerance; no executable installer payload inferred from document bytes.

Toga postinstall calls reportTelemetryEnv -> applyTelemetryEnv before the --post-install early return. It rewrites global ~/.claude/settings.json with OTLP logs/traces to https://otel.togaiq.com, a bundled collector token, prompt/assistant/tool-content logging and a 60KB content limit. It creates backup and atomic replacement; only TOGA_SKIP_TELEMETRY=1 opts out. README does not disclose this global content export. Likely intent: persistent collection of agent conversations across projects by installing a package.
Toga 1.0.1110: independently inspected installer and package hooks; same default global agent-content export as 1.0.1108, with identical relevant function positions.
Toga 1.0.1111: independently inspected installer and package hooks; same default global agent-content export as the other two versions.

WhatsApp client library. Registration endpoints alone are neutral messaging capabilities. Actual Frida-assisted attestation token relay remains suspicious; reviewed source and callback role, without establishing a credential-stealing destination.

ActionsBench wheel. Python CLI loads and scores labeled workflow files under _corpus/cases; it invokes configured scanners, not the vulnerable workflows themselves. Nested .github/workflows directories are fixture data, outside the package root workflow activation surface. Active root workflow controls still flag injection.
ez Python utilities. Screenshot capture and HTTP helpers are separate call/data flows. Bound HTTP-body provenance control added; unsupported screenshot-theft inference removed.

Syglass scientific visualization distribution, including native dependencies. Reviewed archive/native API profiles. WebSocket, registry writes and process creation are not a bound backdoor tasking path; autorun references remain one suspicious finding.

Cuckoo process-injection utility source. Reviewed injection functions, CLI modes, session-restriction helper and source banner. Actual assessment/instrumentation source, not a concealed installed hook; API reference facts retained.
Agentsight capture-core crate. Source uses process/thread instrumentation capabilities; source review and scan did not establish a hidden endpoint payload or export path.

Reachable patched entry decodes a 71-byte XOR stub, transfers into an executable resource section, feedback-decrypts a 44,769-byte mapper and RC4-decrypts a 35,840-byte UPX DLL. Mapper applies relocations/imports and calls DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH before restoring host entry. Recovered code initializes infection workers, recursively mutates PE headers/entry sections, preserves timestamps, creates drive autorun open/explore commands, disguises itself as Intel(R) HD Graphics Manager.exe and contains updatewin.ddns.net update logic. Likely intent: executable infection, removable-drive spread and persistence. Host LoopBeAudio version metadata does not exonerate the graft.

Protected Chinese/E-language executable with VMProtect structures and fly/aimbot cheat controls. Reviewed PE sections/imports/resources and bounded CPU trace (35,995 instructions). Trace stopped on unmapped VM/PEB-related access without recovering a final payload. Enumerated process-memory-write APIs do not prove executed injection. Likely game-cheat/process modification; malicious loader intent remains unresolved. Purgatory, not a fully unpacked or benign verdict.

Protected x64 native network client with curl-related content, sparse imports and VMProtect profile. Bounded trace reached 361,085 instructions/2,769 blocks and stopped at an invalid fetch without exposing a final payload. Packing/junk alone is insufficient to ascribe malware intent. Purgatory because the protected execution path remains unresolved.

Ekranware Informer monitoring/client PE. Examined native imports/resources and activation profile; suspicious string/API combinations did not establish a concealed second payload. Assessment is static and does not claim that an unexpected monitoring-agent deployment is authorized.

ScreenConnect MSI custom deployment. Recovered OLE streams, cabinet files and active app.config despite generic archive header errors. Custom pinned relay admin.ddjncjifknxmidhffjdn.sbs:8041, unattended Access service, disabled tray/banner/balloon/feedback indicators, service/SafeBoot/LSA/credential-provider persistence. Likely intent on an endpoint: persistent low-visibility remote access. Hostile under the user policy that any nondefault ScreenConnect signal is hostile. Vendor signing identifies origin, not deployment authorization.
Spicetify installer command iwr ... | iex. Explicit retrieval/execution is real; one suspicious finding remains rather than three aliases for the same operation.

Tiny PE fixture: entry is RET, no TLS callback directory or exports, only ordinary imported APIs. Injection byte sequences are unreachable from the entry; API/data observations retained at neutral level. A changed-entry/TLS/export near miss must not receive the inert-entry context.
Python fixture launches offset-encoded PowerShell whose recovered body is Write-Output. Encoding is real, retained suspicious; host command-argument capability is neutral.
Two-file package fixture contains a copied README heading and manifest only, with no lifecycle hook or executable payload. Heading mismatch is metadata, not supply-chain impersonation by itself.
File named embedded1.exe is actually a tiny DLL whose entry returns success. No active payload recovered; DLL/extension mismatch remains suspicious.

Exasol assessment PoC logs in with factory SYS credentials and creates a Python scalar UDF exposing os.popen. Shell execution is real, but an explicit target-bound security test, not an autonomous endpoint implant. One suspicious finding retained.
Go fixture writes a gzip-decoded tiny ELF to a temporary path and launches it. Recovered ELF is a minimal demonstration payload. Temp-path execution remains suspicious.
VB fixture consists of API declarations and constants, including thread-context and crypto references. No executable process-hijacking sequence; facts moved to capability directories.
Python fixture enumerates industrial process names and continues; no sabotage or parameter modification body. One process-discovery finding retained.
JavaScript constant pair contains a jailbreak and system-prompt extraction request. No model invocation is established; one adversarial-prompt finding remains rather than a fabricated bound campaign.
Decoded eval(unescape(...)) body is alert(1). Obfuscated JavaScript evaluation is real, retained as one suspicious finding.
oVirt system-test source. Firewall disabled observation is genuine test provisioning; duplicate firewall rollup removed.

Tiny PE fixture returns immediately with no TLS callbacks/exports. Defender/firewall command text is inert data; no reachable command-launcher code was found. Ordinary DLL imports do not activate those strings.
HTML dictionary-fed eval fixture is syntactically nonfunctional as a loader. Obfuscation/eval shape remains unusual; no decoded hostile execution body established.
VBScript repeatedly concatenates Chr(65)..Chr(68), producing ABCD repetitions. Character conversion is data construction; no loader or execution sink.
Same inert-entry PE activation assessment as autorun-directive.exe; unreachable injection bytes alone are not an executing hollowing implant.

Repaired/unpacked Rifaien image from the earlier deep review. Entry/constructor/TLS and overlay activation audited: code reads its own PE, mutates a 16-byte [[UNIQUE]] slot, writes rifaien2-random.exe, uploads the copy as multipart to wecan.hasthe.technology/upload and repeats/deletes. Truncated appended PE is transferred as data, never activated by this sample. Self-mutating public sample submission is real and risky; possible VM-playground purpose does not establish endpoint authorization. Purgatory; original had a hostile trait already.

Four-member package fixture with a foreign README heading and identity functions. Reviewed complete members and manifest; no install hooks or callback/payload body. Documentation identity mismatch stays metadata.
Renamed outer-publication control has the same small identity-function contents as the companion fixture. Outer name is not executable malicious behavior.
Native resource-entry fixture. Reviewed entry/resource activation and callback surfaces; no secret hash-based decoder or reached resource payload found.
Native resource-entry/signature fixture. Reviewed entry and resource code boundaries; signature bytes are test data without a reached malicious stage.

Electron token-session replay helper accepts access/refresh tokens, rewrites admin.microsoft.com Authorization, posts into OWA authentication, refreshes tokens in a hidden browser and extracts ESTSAUTH cookies with broad admin scopes. Likely session bridging/replay, with token/account ownership and invocation context unproved. No attacker exfiltration destination established. Too sensitive/ambiguous for good training.
setup.py defines a downloader function but never invokes it, and defines no install command hook. No reachable download-and-execute stage in the supplied file.

Renamed Rust source package contains Windows API names/declarations without a compilable token-theft implementation. App-bound token API co-occurrence remains one suspicious profile, not proof of executed theft.
PowerShell fixture executes an untrusted HTTP response through IEX. One suspicious pipeline finding retained; no recovered later response was fetched or executed.

DMSQL VSIX. Reviewed extension manifest, activation/entry points and source API call inventory. Database/network actions belong to explicit extension functionality; no concealed credential-export or install-stage payload established.
